title: History & Modern Iran
intro: Iran’s past unfolds through archaeological landscapes, changing dynasties and everyday social experience. Follow the connections between ancient settlements, modern political transformations and the people who shaped them.

children.title: Ancient Civilizations
children.intro: Cities, burial grounds and excavated objects reveal Iran before the great imperial narratives. Archaeology connects these places through settlement, craft and exchange.

children.title: Elam
children.intro: Elam was an ancient civilization of southwestern Iran. Susa provides an important point of entry into its material history.

children.title: Jiroft Civilization
children.intro: Jiroft brings southeastern Iran into discussions of early settlement. Carved objects and archaeological contexts invite attention to craft and exchange.

children.title: Shahr-e Sukhteh
children.intro: Shahr-e Sukhteh preserves traces of an early urban settlement. Buildings, burials and everyday objects illuminate life beyond royal histories.

children.title: Marlik Civilization
children.intro: Marlik is associated with ancient burial grounds and finely worked objects. Its material culture foregrounds metalwork and ceremonial display.

children.title: Tepe Sialk
children.intro: Tepe Sialk contains successive layers of ancient settlement near Kashan. Archaeological remains connect architecture, ceramics and changing forms of community.

children.title: Archaeological Sites of Lorestan
children.intro: Lorestan’s archaeological sites offer perspectives on settlement and skilled metalworking. Their local contexts matter as much as individual objects.

children.title: Ancient Persian Empires
children.intro: Imperial history connects administration, warfare, trade and visual culture across large territories. The differences between these empires are as revealing as their shared legacies.

children.title: Achaemenid Empire
children.intro: The Achaemenid Empire brought diverse territories into an imperial framework. Persepolis offers a distinctive view of its ceremonial architecture.

children.title: Parthian Empire
children.intro: The Parthian Empire connects Iranian history with wider continental exchanges. Its political landscape included powerful regional centers and aristocratic networks.

children.title: Sasanian Empire
children.intro: The Sasanian Empire preceded the medieval transformation of Iran. Court culture, rock reliefs and administrative traditions are central to its historical study.

children.title: Medes
children.intro: The Medes appear in accounts of early Iranian political formations. Textual evidence and archaeology offer different approaches to their history.

children.title: Medieval Iran
children.intro: Medieval Iran was shaped by changing dynasties and regional centers. Persian writing, urban life and artistic exchange developed across overlapping political worlds.

children.title: Tahirid Dynasty
children.intro: The Tahirids belong to the political history of medieval eastern Iran. Their regional government offers context for later dynastic developments.

children.title: Saffarid Dynasty
children.intro: The Saffarids emerged in Sistan. Their story connects regional military power with the changing political geography of medieval Iran.

children.title: Samanid Dynasty
children.intro: The Samanids are associated with eastern Iranian court culture. Persian literary production provides an important route into their historical legacy.

children.title: Ghaznavid Dynasty
children.intro: The Ghaznavids governed from a wider eastern political sphere. Their courts connected military expansion, patronage and literary activity.

children.title: Seljuk Empire
children.intro: The Seljuks linked Iranian centers with a wider imperial geography. Administration and architectural patronage illuminate their period.

children.title: Khwarazmian Empire
children.intro: The Khwarazmian Empire occupied a changing medieval crossroads. Its history connects regional power with the upheavals surrounding Mongol expansion.

children.title: Ilkhanate
children.intro: The Ilkhanate formed part of the Mongol political world. Its Iranian history includes administrative adaptation and artistic exchange.

children.title: Timurid Empire
children.intro: Timurid courts supported elaborate artistic and architectural production. Their cultural networks extended across Iranian and Central Asian centers.

children.title: Later Iranian Dynasties
children.intro: Later dynasties reshaped territorial power, urban centers and relations with other states. Courtly production and everyday social change offer complementary perspectives on these periods.

children.title: Safavid Dynasty
children.intro: The Safavid period reshaped Iran’s political and urban landscape. Isfahan’s courtly architecture provides one perspective on its legacy.

children.title: Afsharid Dynasty
children.intro: The Afsharid dynasty is associated with Nader Shah. Military campaigns and the challenges of maintaining political authority frame its history.

children.title: Zand Dynasty
children.intro: The Zand period connects especially with Shiraz. Urban building and regional governance offer ways to understand its legacy.

children.title: Qajar Dynasty
children.intro: The Qajar period brought changing relations with foreign powers and domestic reform movements. Photography and urban development also transformed cultural life.

children.title: Pahlavi Dynasty
children.intro: The Pahlavi period connects state-building with extensive social and economic change. Its modernization projects remain subjects of historical debate.

children.title: Modern Political Transformations
children.intro: Modern political history includes struggles over representation, sovereignty and state authority. These events are presented as historical subjects rather than political endorsements.

children.title: Russo-Persian Wars
children.intro: The Russo-Persian wars reshaped northern frontiers and diplomatic relationships. Treaties and military reform are central to their historical context.

children.title: Constitutional Revolution
children.intro: The Constitutional Revolution centered on limits to power and representative government. Its debates linked political reform with a changing public sphere.

children.title: Oil Nationalization
children.intro: Oil nationalization connected resource ownership with national sovereignty. Its history brings labor, diplomacy and state revenue into the same discussion.

children.title: The 1953 Coup
children.intro: The 1953 coup altered Iran’s political direction. Understanding it requires attention to domestic conflicts and international intervention.

children.title: The 1979 Revolution
children.intro: The 1979 Revolution transformed Iran’s political order. Its history includes diverse participants, competing expectations and far-reaching institutional change.

children.title: Iran–Iraq War
children.intro: The Iran–Iraq War affected cities, borderlands and everyday lives. Its human consequences extend beyond military and diplomatic histories.

children.title: Political Developments after 1979
children.intro: Political developments after 1979 include institutional consolidation and recurring public debate. Different periods require their own historical context.

children.title: Economic History
children.intro: Economic history follows the circulation of goods, resources and money. Trade routes and productive institutions connect local livelihoods with wider political change.

children.title: Silk Road & Historical Trade
children.intro: Silk Road exchanges connected Iranian places with distant commercial networks. Goods circulated alongside techniques, stories and cultural practices.

children.title: History of Oil Extraction
children.intro: Oil extraction changed industrial landscapes and public finance. Its history also involves workers, technology and foreign relations.

children.title: History of Industrial Production
children.intro: Industrial production moved work into new organizational settings. Factory histories reveal machinery, skills and changing labor relations.

children.title: History of Banking
children.intro: Banking history traces institutions that organized deposits, credit and payment. Their development accompanied changing commercial practices.

children.title: Money & Coinage
children.intro: Coins combine practical exchange with visual statements of authority. Materials, inscriptions and circulation connect money to its historical setting.

children.title: History of Foreign Trade
children.intro: Foreign trade histories track changing routes, partners and goods. Ports, border markets and merchants make those exchanges visible.

children.title: Social History
children.intro: Social history looks beyond rulers to the organization of everyday life. Households, settlements and movement reveal how communities experienced larger changes.

children.title: History of Urbanization
children.intro: Urbanization describes the growth and transformation of towns. Housing, work and shared services reveal its social consequences.

children.title: Villages & Rural Life
children.intro: Rural histories center villages, agricultural work and local relationships. Changes in land and mobility reshape community life.

children.title: History of Nomadic Life
children.intro: Nomadic life connects mobile households with seasonal landscapes. Its history involves pastoral knowledge, exchange and relations with settled communities.

children.title: Families & Social Change
children.intro: Family histories examine household structures and relationships. Social change becomes visible through marriage, care and generational expectations.

children.title: History of Public Education
children.intro: Public education expanded the settings in which knowledge was shared. School histories also reveal access, language and social aspiration.

children.title: Internal Migration through History
children.intro: Internal migration moved people between regions and settlement types. Its history links employment, family networks and changing urban life.

children.title: History of Science & Technology
children.intro: Knowledge has traveled through texts, workshops, schools and instruments. The history of technology also includes the skills of makers and the practical problems they addressed.

children.title: Ancient Centers of Learning
children.intro: Ancient learning centers connected instruction with specialist knowledge. Their study depends on material remains and surviving written evidence.

children.title: History of Medicine
children.intro: Medical history follows changing understandings of health and treatment. Texts, training and care settings offer different kinds of evidence.

children.title: Engineering & Architecture through History
children.intro: Engineering and architecture turn practical knowledge into built form. Historical structures reveal materials, techniques and environmental adaptation.

children.title: Astronomy & Mathematics through History
children.intro: Astronomy and mathematics developed through observation, calculation and teaching. Instruments and manuscripts preserve parts of these intellectual traditions.

children.title: History of Printing
children.intro: Printing changed the reproduction and circulation of texts. Workshops and publishing networks helped reshape reading cultures.

children.title: History of Communication Technologies
children.intro: Communication technologies changed how information traveled. Postal systems, telegraphy and later media belong to different historical settings.

children.title: Historical Figures
children.intro: Historical figures are understood through their works, decisions and surviving evidence. Their reputations also change as later generations reinterpret the past.

children.title: Cyrus the Great
children.intro: Cyrus founded the Achaemenid imperial dynasty. His historical legacy connects political expansion with enduring narratives of kingship.

children.title: Darius the Great
children.intro: Darius consolidated Achaemenid rule through administration and monumental building. Inscriptions provide an important perspective on his representation of power.

children.title: Ardashir I
children.intro: Ardashir I founded the Sasanian dynasty. His rise marks a significant transition in ancient Iranian political history.

children.title: Ferdowsi
children.intro: Ferdowsi composed the Shahnameh. Its epic storytelling has shaped Persian literary memory across generations.

children.title: Nizam al-Mulk
children.intro: Nizam al-Mulk is associated with medieval statecraft and administration. His political writing offers a window onto ideas of government.

children.title: Amir Kabir
children.intro: Amir Kabir is remembered for reform during the Qajar period. Education and administrative change are central to his public legacy.

children.title: Abbas Mirza
children.intro: Abbas Mirza is associated with Qajar military reform. His historical context includes warfare and changing relations with neighboring powers.

children.title: Mohammad Mosaddegh
children.intro: Mohammad Mosaddegh is closely associated with oil nationalization. Parliamentary politics and sovereignty frame discussions of his career.

children.title: Influential Scientific & Cultural Figures
children.intro: Scientific and cultural figures leave different kinds of evidence. Works, correspondence and institutions help situate their individual contributions.

title: People, Values & Culture
intro: Culture lives in conversation, shared meals and the things people make. Languages, celebrations and regional traditions reveal many ways of belonging within Iran.

children.title: Iranian Identity
children.intro: Identity brings shared histories into conversation with regional differences. Names, symbols and everyday attachments reveal how belonging is expressed and debated.

children.title: The Idea of Iranian Identity
children.intro: Iranian identity combines historical memory with lived belonging. Its meaning varies across places, generations and individual experiences.

children.title: National Symbols
children.intro: National symbols give shared ideas visible form. Literature, landscapes and cultural objects can carry symbolic significance.

children.title: Historical Flags of Iran
children.intro: Historical flags record changing political symbols. Their study concerns visual history rather than the display of present-day state emblems.

children.sourceTitle: نام ایران و تحول تاریخی آن
children.title: The Name Iran through History
children.intro: The name Iran has its own linguistic and historical development. Changes in usage connect naming with geography and collective identity.

children.title: National & Local Identities
children.intro: National and local identities can coexist in everyday life. Language, place and family memory give belonging multiple scales.

children.title: Languages & Dialects
children.intro: Iran’s linguistic landscape includes distinct languages and local varieties. Speech carries literature, oral memory and the texture of everyday relationships.

children.title: Persian
children.intro: Persian connects written literature with many spoken varieties. Its contemporary use spans education, media and everyday communication.

children.title: Azerbaijani & Azeri Languages
children.intro: Azeri and Azerbaijani require attention to linguistic terminology. Historical Iranian varieties and contemporary Turkic Azerbaijani are distinct subjects.

children.title: Kurdish
children.intro: Kurdish includes several linguistic varieties. Poetry, music and everyday speech preserve different regional traditions.

children.title: Luri
children.intro: Luri belongs to Iran’s linguistic diversity. Local speech connects community histories with oral expression.

children.title: Gilaki
children.intro: Gilaki is spoken in parts of the Caspian region. Its oral traditions connect language with local life.

children.title: Mazandarani
children.intro: Mazandarani forms part of the northern linguistic landscape. Songs and everyday expression carry its regional character.

children.title: Balochi
children.intro: Balochi connects communities across southeastern Iran and neighboring regions. Oral poetry is an important part of its cultural expression.

children.title: Turkmen
children.intro: Turkmen belongs to the Turkic language family. Local storytelling and music offer routes into its Iranian cultural settings.

children.title: Talysh
children.intro: Talysh is associated with communities along the southwestern Caspian region. Local varieties preserve distinctive linguistic traditions.

children.title: Local Dialects
children.intro: Local dialects reveal fine-grained differences in speech. Vocabulary and pronunciation often reflect long histories of interaction.

children.title: Social Customs
children.intro: Social customs shape the small gestures of daily relationships. Their expression changes with setting, generation and the familiarity between people.

children.title: Hospitality
children.intro: Hospitality makes welcoming others a social practice. Food, tea and time together give it everyday form.

children.title: Taarof
children.intro: Taarof is a language of courtesy and social negotiation. Meaning depends on context rather than literal wording alone.

children.title: Visiting Customs
children.intro: Visiting customs organize encounters between households. Greetings, refreshments and timing express attention to the relationship.

children.title: Gift Giving
children.intro: Gift giving marks affection, gratitude and important occasions. The gesture’s meaning depends on the people and setting.

children.title: Wedding Traditions
children.intro: Wedding traditions combine family participation with celebration. Practices differ across regions and contemporary lifestyles.

children.title: Secular Mourning Traditions
children.intro: Secular mourning traditions express loss through shared remembrance. Gatherings and acts of support sustain relationships around bereavement.

children.title: Everyday Social Etiquette
children.intro: Everyday etiquette guides greetings, requests and respectful conversation. Familiarity and circumstance shape what feels appropriate.

children.title: Cultural Celebrations
children.intro: Seasonal celebrations connect calendars with memory and social gathering. Food, storytelling and shared preparations give each occasion a distinctive atmosphere.

children.title: Nowruz
children.intro: Nowruz marks the arrival of spring in the Iranian calendar. Household preparations and visits connect renewal with social relationships.

children.title: Chaharshanbe Suri
children.intro: Chaharshanbe Suri is associated with the approach of Nowruz. Fire and neighborhood gathering form part of its familiar imagery.

children.title: Yalda Night
children.intro: Yalda Night celebrates the longest night of the year. Fruit, poetry and conversation bring people together.

children.title: Sadeh
children.intro: Sadeh is a midwinter celebration associated with fire. Its cultural memory connects seasonal change with communal gathering.

children.title: Mehregan
children.intro: Mehregan draws on an ancient seasonal tradition. Contemporary observances connect cultural memory with celebration.

children.title: Local & Seasonal Celebrations
children.intro: Local celebrations reflect regional calendars and livelihoods. Harvests and seasonal transitions provide occasions to gather.

children.title: Family & Lifestyle
children.intro: Households organize care, resources and everyday routines. Family life changes alongside housing, education and generational expectations.

children.title: Iranian Family Structures
children.intro: Iranian families take varied household forms. Relationships of care extend across and beyond the home.

children.title: Intergenerational Relationships
children.intro: Intergenerational relationships connect different memories and expectations. Daily support often travels in both directions.

children.title: Changing Lifestyles
children.intro: Lifestyles change with work, technology and patterns of residence. Everyday routines reveal these shifts more clearly than broad labels.

children.title: Youth Culture
children.intro: Youth culture includes changing forms of leisure and self-expression. Music, style and digital spaces provide visible settings.

children.title: Single & Family Life
children.intro: Single and family households organize time and space differently. Housing and support networks shape both experiences.

children.title: Apartment Living
children.intro: Apartment living involves shared buildings and negotiated routines. Noise, maintenance and common spaces make neighborly relationships practical.

children.title: Rural Lifestyles
children.intro: Rural lifestyles connect households with local landscapes and work. Modern services and mobility also influence village routines.

children.title: Regional & Ethnic Cultures
children.intro: Regional cultures are living practices rather than fixed categories. Language, food, dress and performance reveal both shared connections and local distinctions.

children.title: Kurdish Culture
children.intro: Kurdish culture includes diverse regional expressions. Music, language and collective celebrations provide distinctive points of encounter.

children.title: Azerbaijani Culture
children.intro: Azerbaijani culture connects speech, storytelling and musical traditions. Local settings give shared practices different expressions.

children.title: Gilaki & Mazandarani Culture
children.intro: Gilaki and Mazandarani cultures reflect northern regional experiences. Food and performance connect them with Caspian landscapes.

children.title: Luri & Bakhtiari Culture
children.intro: Luri and Bakhtiari cultures include rich musical and oral traditions. Mobility and regional histories contribute to their variety.

children.title: Baloch Culture
children.intro: Baloch culture includes embroidery, music and oral storytelling. These practices connect makers and performers across generations.

children.title: Turkmen Culture
children.intro: Turkmen culture brings textile traditions into conversation with music and storytelling. Local communities sustain and reinterpret those forms.

children.title: Iranian Arab Culture
children.intro: Iranian Arab culture includes distinctive linguistic and artistic traditions. Southern regional histories shape its varied expressions.

children.title: Qashqai Culture
children.intro: Qashqai culture connects woven objects, music and community memory. Pastoral mobility forms one part of its broader social history.

children.title: Food & Cooking
children.intro: Cooking translates landscape and household knowledge into shared meals. Regional ingredients and methods reveal a cuisine with many local voices.

children.title: Traditional Iranian Dishes
children.intro: Traditional dishes combine practiced techniques with familiar ingredients. Family recipes preserve variation within recognizable forms.

children.title: Regional Cuisines
children.intro: Regional cuisines reflect local produce and histories of exchange. A dish’s preparation may change from one place to another.

children.title: Traditional Breads
children.intro: Traditional breads differ in dough, shape and baking surface. Bakeries make these skills part of everyday public life.

children.title: Iranian Sweets
children.intro: Iranian sweets connect pastry skills with occasions of hospitality. Nuts, spices and textures create regional distinctions.

children.title: Tea Culture
children.intro: Tea drinking gives conversation an everyday rhythm. Preparation and serving are part of the social experience.

children.title: Seasonal Foods
children.intro: Seasonal foods follow the availability of ingredients. Their return can become a marker of time and memory.

children.title: Secular Ceremonial Foods
children.intro: Ceremonial foods accompany secular celebrations and gatherings. Cooking gives shared occasions a material and sensory form.

children.title: Clothing & Everyday Crafts
children.intro: Clothing and useful objects carry the knowledge of their makers. Materials, patterns and repeated hand movements connect craft with everyday life.

children.title: Regional Dress
children.intro: Regional dress expresses local histories through fabric and form. Contemporary use ranges from daily wear to special occasions.

children.title: Local Textile Weaving
children.intro: Local textile weaving joins pattern with the structure of cloth. Fibers and techniques reflect available materials and learned skills.

children.title: Kilim & Jajim
children.intro: Kilim and jajim are woven textiles with distinctive structures. Pattern emerges through the arrangement of colored threads.

children.title: Carpet Weaving
children.intro: Carpet weaving builds a surface through repeated knots. Design and making connect household knowledge with specialist production.

children.title: Basket Weaving
children.intro: Basket weaving turns flexible plant materials into useful forms. Local environments influence both technique and appearance.

children.title: Traditional Pottery
children.intro: Traditional pottery transforms clay through shaping and firing. Everyday vessels connect practical needs with decoration.

children.title: Wooden Handicrafts
children.intro: Wooden handicrafts reveal carving, joining and surface finishing skills. Useful objects can also carry local visual traditions.

children.title: Oral Traditions & Folklore
children.intro: Spoken traditions move through repetition and variation. Stories, songs and games carry memory while adapting to new listeners and settings.

children.title: Persian Proverbs
children.intro: Persian proverbs condense observation into memorable expressions. Their force depends on when and how they are used.

children.title: Folk Tales
children.intro: Folk tales travel through retelling rather than a single fixed text. Performers adapt characters and details to their listeners.

children.title: Iranian Legends
children.intro: Iranian legends link extraordinary events with places and figures. Different versions reveal the flexibility of cultural memory.

children.title: Ancient Iranian Myths
children.intro: Ancient myths offer symbolic stories about origins and conflict. Later art and literature continue to reinterpret them.

children.title: Traditional Games
children.intro: Traditional games organize play through shared rules. Local variations connect recreation with community life.

children.title: Folk Songs
children.intro: Folk songs carry stories and rhythms across generations. Performance gives language an emotional and collective setting.

children.title: Pahlavani Traditions
children.intro: Pahlavani traditions connect physical practice with ideas of character. Storytelling and public memory contribute to their cultural meaning.

children.title: Contemporary Everyday Culture
children.intro: Contemporary culture develops through ordinary decisions and encounters. Workplaces, neighborhoods and digital settings provide different spaces for changing values.

children.title: Urban Culture
children.intro: Urban culture emerges from living together at close quarters. Streets, services and public encounters shape its routines.

children.title: Consumer Culture
children.intro: Consumer culture concerns the meanings attached to goods. Taste and aspiration influence purchases alongside practical need.

children.title: Work Culture
children.intro: Work culture includes expectations about responsibility and cooperation. Everyday practices give formal organizations their lived character.

children.title: Social Cooperation
children.intro: Social cooperation brings people together around shared tasks. Trust and repeated participation help sustain collective efforts.

children.title: Volunteering
children.intro: Volunteering contributes time and skills outside ordinary paid work. Community needs give these activities their local shape.

children.title: Online Culture
children.intro: Online culture develops through digital conversation and expression. Platforms influence how communities form and share material.

children.title: Changing Social Values
children.intro: Social values change through debate and lived experience. Differences between generations can make those shifts especially visible.

title: Nature & Geography
intro: Mountains, inland basins and contrasting coastlines give Iran a varied physical character. Water, vegetation and settlement connect these landscapes with the experience of living in them.

children.title: Physical Geography
children.intro: The Iranian plateau brings highlands into contact with enclosed basins. Its physical structure helps explain contrasts in climate and settlement.

children.title: Iranian Plateau
children.intro: The Iranian plateau is a broad highland region. Mountains and interior basins give it varied relief.

children.title: Alborz Mountains
children.intro: The Alborz runs south of the Caspian Sea. Its slopes create strong environmental contrasts.

children.title: Zagros Mountains
children.intro: The Zagros extends across western and southwestern Iran. Folded ridges shape valleys and movement.

children.title: Dasht-e Kavir
children.intro: Dasht-e Kavir occupies part of the central plateau. Salt surfaces and aridity define its landscape.

children.title: Lut Desert
children.intro: The Lut is a southeastern desert region. Wind-shaped landforms give it a distinctive terrain.

children.title: Central Plains
children.intro: Central plains lie between highland systems. Water availability strongly influences their use and settlement.

children.title: Seas & Lakes
children.intro: Large bodies of water frame Iran’s north and south while inland lakes occupy distinct basins. Their ecologies depend on connections between water, land and climate.

children.title: Caspian Sea
children.intro: The Caspian is an enclosed inland sea. Iran’s northern coast belongs to its wider basin.

children.title: Persian Gulf
children.intro: The Persian Gulf lies south of Iran. Coastal communities and islands connect land with maritime routes.

children.title: Gulf of Oman
children.intro: The Gulf of Oman opens toward the Arabian Sea. Its coastline gives southeastern Iran a maritime horizon.

children.title: Lake Urmia
children.intro: Lake Urmia occupies a northwestern basin. Salinity and changing water levels shape its environmental story.

children.title: Hamun Lakes
children.intro: The Hamun lakes form a connected wetland landscape. Their conditions depend on water reaching the Sistan basin.

children.title: Namak Lake
children.intro: Namak Lake is a salt lake of the interior. Seasonal water and exposed salt create changing surfaces.

children.title: Rivers & Water Resources
children.intro: Rivers connect mountain catchments with settlements and cultivated land. Reservoirs and springs add different scales to the geography of water.

children.title: Karun River
children.intro: The Karun drains part of the Zagros. Its basin links mountain water with southwestern lowlands.

children.title: Zayandeh Rud
children.intro: The Zayandeh Rud connects upland catchments with central Iran. Its changing flow matters to communities and landscapes.

children.title: Sefidrud River
children.intro: The Sefidrud reaches the Caspian coast. Its basin connects highland terrain with northern lowlands.

children.title: Aras River
children.intro: The Aras follows parts of Iran’s northwestern frontier. Valleys along its course connect water with borderland life.

children.title: Karkheh River
children.intro: The Karkheh is a southwestern river system. Its catchment links Zagros landscapes with lower plains.

children.title: Helmand River
children.intro: The Helmand carries water toward the Sistan basin. Its cross-border catchment is central to regional water discussions.

children.title: Dams & Reservoirs
children.intro: Dams impound water while reservoirs store it. Their effects extend through river systems and surrounding settlements.

children.title: Springs & Waterfalls
children.intro: Springs emerge where groundwater reaches the surface. Waterfalls reveal abrupt changes in terrain along flowing water.

children.title: Forests & Vegetation
children.intro: Vegetation responds to moisture, altitude and seasonal conditions. Iran’s wooded landscapes range from broadleaf forests to oak country and coastal mangroves.

children.title: Hyrcanian Forests
children.intro: Hyrcanian forests follow the southern Caspian slopes. Broadleaf woodland gives the region a distinctive green character.

children.title: Zagros Forests
children.intro: Zagros forests include extensive oak landscapes. Seasonal conditions influence their structure and regeneration.

children.title: Arasbaran Forests
children.intro: Arasbaran combines woodland with varied upland habitats. Its vegetation reflects a meeting of different environmental influences.

children.title: Hara Mangroves
children.intro: Hara mangroves occupy tidal coastal environments. Their roots connect woodland ecology with marine processes.

children.title: Rangelands
children.intro: Rangelands support vegetation adapted to grazing landscapes. Their condition connects land management with pastoral livelihoods.

children.title: Native Plant Species
children.intro: Native plants belong to local ecological histories. Habitat and climate help explain their distribution.

children.title: Deserts & Drylands
children.intro: Arid environments are shaped by the balance between water, wind and exposed material. Dunes, salt surfaces and erosion reveal different processes within that balance.

children.title: Maranjab Desert
children.intro: Maranjab offers dune and salt-flat landscapes near Kashan. Wind leaves fine patterns across exposed sand.

children.title: Mesr Desert
children.intro: Mesr is associated with desert settlement and dune landscapes. Local life provides a human scale to arid terrain.

children.title: Dasht-e Lut
children.intro: Dasht-e Lut contains varied desert landforms. Wind erosion and deposition shape its striking surfaces.

children.title: Sistan Deserts
children.intro: Sistan’s drylands combine exposed terrain with a changing wetland context. Wind and water availability influence their character.

children.title: Desertification
children.intro: Desertification describes land degradation in dry regions. Soil, vegetation and land use interact in the process.

children.title: Soil Erosion
children.intro: Soil erosion removes and transports surface material. Water, wind and vegetation cover influence its pace.

children.title: Mountains & Highlands
children.intro: Mountain landscapes vary with rock, elevation and exposure. Peaks also belong to wider systems of valleys, water and seasonal movement.

children.title: Damavand
children.intro: Damavand is a volcanic mountain in the Alborz. Its prominent form carries strong cultural associations.

children.title: Alam Kuh
children.intro: Alam Kuh belongs to the high Alborz. Steep rock and alpine terrain define its landscape.

children.title: Sabalan
children.intro: Sabalan is a northwestern volcanic massif. High-altitude conditions give its upper slopes a distinct environment.

children.title: Zard Kuh
children.intro: Zard Kuh forms part of the Zagros highlands. Ridges and seasonal snow shape its mountain setting.

children.title: Dena
children.intro: Dena is a massif within the Zagros. Its connected ridges create a complex upland landscape.

children.title: Alborz & Zagros Ranges
children.intro: Alborz and Zagros are different mountain systems. Their orientation helps structure Iran’s physical geography.

children.title: Islands & Coasts
children.intro: Island and coastal environments connect terrestrial landscapes with the sea. Shores also sustain settlements, work and distinctive cultural traditions.

children.title: Qeshm Island
children.intro: Qeshm lies in the Persian Gulf. Geology and tidal environments contribute to its varied landscapes.

children.title: Kish Island
children.intro: Kish is a Persian Gulf island. Coastal recreation and built environments shape its contemporary visitor experience.

children.title: Hormuz Island
children.intro: Hormuz is known for strongly colored geological surfaces. Its island setting places those materials beside the sea.

children.title: Larak Island
children.intro: Larak lies near the Strait of Hormuz. Its coastal landscape forms part of a maritime island region.

children.title: Tunb Islands & Abu Musa
children.intro: The Tunb islands and Abu Musa belong to a disputed maritime context. Geographic description requires distinguishing location from sovereignty claims.

children.title: Makran Coast
children.intro: Makran follows Iran’s southeastern shoreline. Coastal cliffs and maritime settlements give it a distinctive geography.

children.title: Caspian Coast
children.intro: The Caspian coast meets northern plains and forested slopes. Settlement patterns follow this narrow meeting of environments.

children.title: Climate & Weather
children.intro: Iran contains sharply contrasting climate settings. Altitude, latitude and access to moisture produce different seasonal experiences across the country.

children.title: Hot Arid Climate
children.intro: Hot arid conditions combine strong heat with limited precipitation. Water storage and shade become important environmental responses.

children.title: Cold Mountain Climate
children.intro: Cold mountain climates reflect elevation and exposure. Snow and short growing seasons shape local conditions.

children.title: Temperate Humid Climate
children.intro: Temperate humid conditions characterize parts of the Caspian region. Moisture supports a different vegetation pattern from the interior.

children.title: Hot Humid Southern Climate
children.intro: Southern humid heat combines warm conditions with coastal moisture. Buildings and daily routines respond to both.

children.title: Climate Change
children.intro: Climate change alters long-term environmental patterns. Temperature, precipitation and extremes require attention across different time scales.

children.title: Drought & Water Scarcity

children.title: Poverty Indicators
children.intro: Poverty indicators describe disadvantage under chosen thresholds. Definitions influence who appears in the measure.

children.title: Education Data
children.intro: Education statistics connect institutions with participation and outcomes. Counts need context about population and educational pathways.

children.title: School Counts
children.intro: School counts describe institutional availability. They do not directly measure teaching quality.

children.title: School Enrollment
children.intro: Enrollment data records participation in schooling. Attendance and learning require additional evidence.

children.title: University Counts
children.intro: University counts summarize institutions under defined categories. Branches can complicate comparison.

children.title: University Student Statistics
children.intro: Student statistics describe participation in higher education. Discipline and degree level add useful detail.

children.title: Scientific Output
children.intro: Scientific output measures recorded research activity. Quantity alone does not establish research quality.

children.title: Graduate Employment
children.intro: Graduate employment data follows transitions after study. Observation periods affect conclusions.

children.title: Geographic Data
children.intro: Geographic datasets locate information within defined spatial frameworks. Scale and boundary versions influence what comparisons are valid.

children.title: Provincial Boundaries
children.intro: Provincial boundaries define regional geographic units. Changes can affect historical comparisons.

children.title: Administrative Divisions
children.intro: Administrative divisions organize territorial government. Their hierarchy differs from natural regions.

children.title: Road Networks
children.intro: Road data represents routes and connections. Completeness matters for network analysis.

children.title: Watersheds
children.intro: Watersheds group land by drainage relationships. They cross administrative boundaries.

children.title: Protected Areas
children.intro: Protected-area data records designated conservation spaces. Boundaries need current documentation.

children.title: Land Use
children.intro: Land-use data classifies how ground is occupied. Categories depend on the mapping method.

children.title: Environmental Data
children.intro: Environmental measurements vary across space and time. Observation methods are essential context rather than optional technical detail.

children.title: Air Quality
children.intro: Air quality data records selected atmospheric conditions. Sensor placement affects representativeness.

children.title: Annual Rainfall
children.intro: Annual rainfall summarizes precipitation over a year. Local averages can conceal extreme events.

children.title: Water Resources
children.intro: Water-resource data describes stocks or flows. Those measures should not be confused.

children.title: Forest Cover
children.intro: Forest-cover data maps wooded surfaces. Definitions influence what counts as forest.

children.title: Wetland Conditions
children.intro: Wetland data records changing ecological conditions. Seasonal variation requires repeated observation.

children.title: Temperature Changes
children.intro: Temperature data tracks conditions over time. Comparable methods support meaningful trend analysis.

children.title: Business Data
children.intro: Business statistics depend on organizational definitions and reporting coverage. Formal registration does not necessarily demonstrate continuing activity.

children.title: Registered Companies
children.intro: Registered-company data counts official organizational records. Some registered entities may be inactive.

children.title: Active Industries
children.intro: Industry data describes productive activity by category. Classification affects sector comparisons.

children.title: Knowledge-based Companies
children.intro: Knowledge-based company data follows a defined designation. Criteria matter when interpreting totals.

children.title: Startups
children.intro: Startup data concerns developing businesses. Different definitions produce different populations.

children.title: Venture Capital
children.intro: Venture-capital data records particular financing activity. Announcements and completed transactions differ.

children.title: Technology Service Exports
children.intro: Technology export data follows cross-border service activity. Intangible delivery can complicate measurement.

children.title: Tourism Data
children.intro: Tourism statistics describe movement and service capacity. A visit, overnight stay and unique visitor are different units.

children.title: Visitor Statistics
children.intro: Visitor statistics count defined travel events or people. The chosen unit affects interpretation.

children.title: Accommodation Capacity
children.intro: Accommodation capacity measures available lodging provision. Availability does not demonstrate actual occupancy.

children.title: Registered Attractions
children.intro: Attraction registers record formally identified sites. Registration is different from visitor volume.

children.title: Travel Routes
children.intro: Travel-route data connects destinations spatially. Seasonal access affects practical use.

children.title: Domestic Travel Volume
children.intro: Domestic travel volume concerns movement within the country. Trip definitions influence the totals.

children.title: Transport Infrastructure
children.intro: Transport data describes the networks serving travel. Physical capacity and service frequency differ.

children.title: Cultural Data
children.intro: Cultural statistics make selected activities visible through counts. Quantitative measures should be read alongside differences in access and participation.

children.title: Published Books
children.intro: Book data records publications under defined criteria. Editions and titles are different units.

children.title: Nationally Registered Heritage
children.intro: Heritage registers count formally recognized properties. Their categories reflect institutional definitions.

children.title: Museums
children.intro: Museum data describes institutions and collections. Visitor access requires additional information.

children.title: Galleries
children.intro: Gallery data follows exhibition spaces. Commercial and noncommercial models differ.

children.title: Cinema Venues
children.intro: Cinema venue data counts screening locations or screens. Those units should remain distinct.

children.title: Arts Festivals
children.intro: Festival data records organized artistic events. Scale and frequency vary between programs.

children.intro: Trade with Turkey involves varied commercial relationships. Transport connections support cross-border activity.

children.title: Trade with Pakistan
children.intro: Pakistani trade connects southeastern routes with neighboring demand. Border infrastructure affects movement.

children.title: Trade with Central Asia
children.intro: Central Asian trade links several distinct economies. Corridor choices influence access.

children.intro: Persian Gulf trade connects maritime neighbors. Ports and distribution networks shape commercial relationships.

children.title: International Corridors
children.intro: Corridors connect routes rather than functioning as single isolated projects. Their usefulness depends on reliable transfers between transport modes.

children.title: North–South Corridor
children.intro: The North–South Corridor links routes across a broad region. Transfers connect different national transport systems.

children.title: East–West Corridors
children.intro: East–West corridors describe connections across longitudinal routes. Multiple alignments can serve different markets.

children.title: Regional Rail Routes
children.intro: Regional rail routes connect fixed networks across boundaries. Compatibility influences onward movement.

children.title: Road Transit Routes
children.intro: Road transit routes carry goods between jurisdictions. Border procedures affect journey continuity.

children.title: Transit Ports
children.intro: Transit ports transfer goods between maritime and inland routes. Terminal coordination supports onward delivery.

children.title: Regional Logistics Networks
children.intro: Regional logistics networks combine storage and movement. Shared information helps coordinate different operators.

children.title: Scientific & Technology Relations
children.intro: Knowledge exchange connects institutions through people and shared work. Sustainable cooperation depends on practical collaboration rather than formal announcements alone.

children.title: Regional University Cooperation
children.intro: University cooperation links academic communities across regions. Joint activity can support teaching and research.

children.title: Software Service Exports
children.intro: Software exports deliver expertise through digital work. Communication supports collaboration across distance.

children.title: Technology Exchange
children.intro: Technology exchange moves tools and experience between organizations. Adaptation matters in new settings.

children.title: Research Cooperation
children.intro: Research cooperation brings complementary expertise to a question. Shared methods help make results comparable.

children.title: Knowledge Transfer
children.intro: Knowledge transfer turns specialist understanding into usable practice. Learning requires more than document delivery.

children.title: Regional Markets for Knowledge-based Products
children.intro: Regional technology markets connect innovation with nearby users. Local requirements shape product adaptation.

children.title: Iranian Diaspora
children.intro: Diaspora experiences vary with destination and generation. Cross-border relationships create multiple forms of professional and cultural connection.

children.title: Iranian Communities in Europe
children.intro: Iranian communities in Europe occupy varied national settings. Local conditions shape their institutions and networks.

children.title: Iranian Communities in North America
children.intro: North American Iranian communities include different migration histories. Generations can experience belonging differently.

children.title: Iranian Communities in Persian Gulf Countries
children.intro: Persian Gulf communities connect residence abroad with regional proximity. Work and family sustain different cross-border relationships.

children.title: Iranian Entrepreneurs Abroad
children.intro: Entrepreneurs abroad build ventures within destination economies. Personal networks can connect several markets.

children.title: Iranian Professionals Abroad
children.intro: Professionals abroad contribute expertise across many fields. Collaboration need not depend on permanent return.

children.title: Scientific & Economic Cooperation Networks
children.intro: Cooperation networks connect scientific and commercial relationships. Shared projects give broad connections practical form.

children.title: Cultural Connections
children.intro: Culture travels through language, objects and performance. International circulation also changes how works are interpreted.

children.title: Persian in Neighboring Countries
children.intro: Persian connects communities beyond national borders. Local literary traditions give the language different voices.

children.title: Persian Literature Worldwide
children.intro: Persian literature reaches readers through translation and study. Interpretation changes across linguistic settings.

children.title: Iranian Handicrafts in Global Markets
children.intro: Handicrafts enter global markets as useful and expressive objects. Provenance supports understanding of makers’ work.

children.title: Iranian Cinema at Festivals
children.intro: Film festivals introduce Iranian cinema to varied audiences. Programming shapes the context of reception.

children.title: Iranian Art in World Museums
children.intro: Iranian art appears within international museum collections. Curatorial choices influence its presentation.

children.title: International Cultural Tourism
children.intro: Cultural tourism brings visitors into contact with lived heritage. Respectful exchange recognizes communities behind the attractions.

children.title: International Cooperation
children.intro: Cooperation brings participants with different needs into shared projects. Clear objectives and practical responsibilities support meaningful exchange.

children.title: Joint Investment
children.intro: Joint investment combines resources from different participants. Governance arrangements shape their working relationship.

children.title: Industrial Product Exports
children.intro: Industrial exports connect manufacturing with overseas use. Product support can continue beyond delivery.

children.title: Technology Service Exports
children.intro: Technology service exports supply expertise across borders. Clear scope supports dependable collaboration.

children.title: University Cooperation
children.intro: University cooperation connects teaching and research institutions. Reciprocal exchange helps sustain partnerships.

children.title: Regional Tourism
children.intro: Regional tourism links nearby destinations and communities. Coordination can make journeys easier to understand.

children.title: Environmental Cooperation
children.intro: Environmental cooperation addresses systems that cross borders. Shared observation supports joint understanding.
